fichas.title: Restaurant kitchen organization
fichas.summary: Restaurant kitchens are organized into hot and cold kitchen areas, a servery, crockery-return and washing areas, and staff facilities. Kitchen layouts and equipment should support efficient production, service, cleaning, and circulation.

Hot kitchens, corresponding to their main functions - cooking and
roasting - contain finishing zones and some or all of the following
equipment: cooker (two to eight rings), increasingly mobile
hotplates, extractor hood, water boiler, fast-cooking equipment,
automatic cooker, steamer, automatic steamer and pressure cooker,
combination device, water bath (bain-marie), baking and roasting
oven, roast and grill plates, frying pans, staged roasting oven, chip
pan, salamander, circulation machine (for frozen goods), microwave
oven, continuous process automatic roaster and baker. Large
automatic appliances are used only in very large kitchens. Storage
and working surfaces should be located between appliances and at
the end of the block. In addition to the fixed arrangement in the block,
mobile appliances are increasingly being used, which can be adapted
better to production changes and are easier to clean. -7 0Cold kitchens should have a layout logically planned in parallel to
the hot kitchen and be convenient for the (common) servery and
bread area. The regular equipment is a day refrigerator under/over
the cold table, various cutting and slicing machines (bread, cold
cuts, meat, cheese), mixing machine, scales, cutting boards, salad
table with lower cold cabinet, toaster or salamander, microwave
oven and sufficient working and storage space -7 0.
Servery for restaurant kitchens with counter or self-service, ideally
situated between the preparation area and the dining room. There
should be sufficient shelf space, a hot cabinet with heated plates
and a cool zone for cold foods. Crockery shelves or upper fixings,
cutlery container. In large businesses, also basket, plate and soup
bowl dispensers.
Crockery return: the difference between washing crockery and
pots is considerable. With waiter service, the plates are brought
back to their own area of the servery -7 0 - 0. In addition to
one or two sinks with drainers, storage space and shelves for
pot washing, small kitchens naturally also require dishwashers
in various sizes, feed types and operational types. Dishwashers
under the worktop are usual, but also tunnel and rotary batch
washers. Provide surfaces for the return (temporary storage,
worktops, sorting, soaking) and space for the crockery -7 0- tD.
Staff area: about 10-15% of the total space required in a kitchen
facility should be allocated for offices and staff rooms. The kitchen
staff will need changing rooms, washing facilities and toilets.
For more than 1 0 employees, a rest/break room is necessary
(workplace regulations). It is important that changing and social
rooms are near the kitchen, to avoid staff having to cross unclean
room areas or corridors. For changing rooms, > 6 m2 floor area,
4-6 air changes per hour and privacy. Provide each employee with
a well-ventilated, lockable cupboard. In large operations, even
differentiate street and working clothes. Guidelines for the toilets:
per unit ryvc and washbasin) 5-6 m2 and for the shower areas
(for more than five male or female employees) a washbasin and
shower, approx. 5.5 m2 per unit.
Ventilation and extraction: according to VDI guideline 2052,
large kitchens should be equipped with mechanical air supply
and extraction. Extract the air at each cooker and run it through
ductwork into the open air. Supply fresh air (no recirculation). Take
the heat production from the appliances into account (e.g. induction
ovens can reduce the unused heating of the surroundings).

fichas.title: Hot kitchen production and equipment
fichas.summary: The hot kitchen is arranged around cooking and roasting functions, with finishing zones and equipment selected for the scale and type of operation. Work and storage surfaces are placed between appliances and at the ends of equipment blocks; mobile appliances allow production layouts to adapt and facilitate cleaning.

dimensions.label: Restaurant capacity
dimensions.context: Kitchen plan caption; production in block

fichas.title: Cold kitchen and servery
fichas.summary: The cold kitchen should be laid out in parallel with the hot kitchen and positioned conveniently for the shared servery and bread area. The servery should sit between preparation and dining, with separate provision for hot and cold foods and sufficient shelving and work space.
furniture_equipment: Salad table with lower cold cabinet

fichas.title: Crockery return, dishwashing and pot washing
fichas.summary: Crockery-return arrangements depend on the service system. Dishwashing areas provide for returns, sorting, waste clearance, pre-washing, washing, discharge, and crockery storage. Pot-washing provision includes sinks, work surfaces, rinsing equipment, shelves, and a holding area.

fichas.title: Ventilation and extraction for large kitchens
fichas.summary: Large kitchens are to have mechanical air supply and extraction in accordance with the cited VDI guideline. Extract air at each cooker and discharge it outdoors; supply fresh air without recirculation, taking appliance heat output into account.
